how: Extracted by scripts/gate_shards.py::parse_failures from the six shard logs of the 2026-09-09 six-shard run at 0ffe68a14 (1181 files). That run predates the committed wrapper and is NOT of record for a pass/fail verdict, but its logs are a faithful capture.
provenance_caveat: ⭐ CORROBORATED AT THE MERGE-BASE — see `corroborated_at_merge_base`. This was originally seeded from a run ON THE BRANCH, which carried the risk that a hub-introduced failure was baked in. That risk is now retired by measurement rather than by argument: a full run at 78ac8016b shows every one of these entries failing at the base too, so none of them is the hub's. The nine FILE names also match the independently-measured branch-base list recorded in RESUME-inc2.md before this work began.

corroborated_at_merge_base.how: Full six-shard run in a detached worktree at the merge-base, using the SAME fixed _capture/parse_failures code as the branch run so the two sets are comparable character for character. Base: 1169 test files, 11 files / 12 tests failing.
corroborated_at_merge_base.result: ZERO entries in this baseline are absent at the merge-base. Every failure the branch carries also fails at the base, so NOTHING in this baseline is hub-introduced. That is the direction that matters and it is clean.
base_only_failures: src/pages/optionsFlow/flowSearchProduct.test.js > the fixture exercises what the matrix claims > CONTROL: heavy and thin tickers both exist, and differ materially
src/pages/screener/sharedScreen.route.test.jsx > the controls that keep the rail honest > exactly one module emits the shared-screen markup
corroborated_at_merge_base.base_only_verdict: ⛔ NOT 'the branch fixed them'. Both were re-run IN ISOLATION at the base and BOTH PASS (10.2s and 2.2s). They are LOAD-SENSITIVE, and the base shards differently from the branch (1169 files vs 1181 moves every shard boundary), so they drew slower neighbours there. Per this repo's standing rule a timeout is never banked as permitted breakage and is re-run alone before it is called anything — so they are NOT added to this baseline. If either appears as a NEW failure in a future run, re-run it alone before treating it as a regression.
